arrangements.title: Cross for a particular purpose
arrangements.note: A repair, meal or leisure trip can cross a border while other parts of life stay put. Illustrative arrangements overlap; this is not a population classification.

arrangements.title: Move home; retain connections
arrangements.note: One participant described lower earnings alongside lower living costs and preferred work. It is an individual account, not a measured general benefit.

arrangements.title: Separate residence and work or study
arrangements.note: Official cross-boundary pupil data illustrate separation of home and school. Mainland residence is not necessarily Shenzhen; the pupil count does not measure workers.

arrangements.title: Stay based in Hong Kong; keep ties elsewhere
arrangements.note: The source account also mentions Shenzhen property. It does not establish a regular commute. Connections can span places without moving home and work.

datasets.title: Movement is visible. People are not counted once.
datasets.eyebrow: HONG KONG RESIDENT DEPARTURES / SIX CHECKPOINTS
datasets.summary: Hong Kong resident departures through six Shenzhen-facing checkpoints increased between these two years.
datasets.caveat: Journeys, not unique people, verified shopping trips or spending. Counts sum Lo Wu, Lok Ma Chau, Lok Ma Chau Spur Line, Man Kam To, Heung Yuen Wai and Shenzhen Bay.

datasets.title: Retail conditions change over time.
datasets.summary: A fall, a modest annual increase and a later partial-year rebound describe different periods.
datasets.caveat: Value, not volume. January–August compares the same months a year earlier and is not annualised. Retail excludes most services and purchases abroad. These figures do not identify Shenzhen as a cause.

datasets.title: Two restaurant categories, different directions.
datasets.summary: The revised official series shows uneven conditions across restaurant categories.
datasets.caveat: Receipt value, not profit or sales volume. Category differences do not identify their causes. The revised +4.1% supersedes +4.0% in an older research note.

datasets.title: An accounting snapshot of room to respond.
datasets.summary: The research calculation is (receipts − employee compensation − operating expenses − cost of goods sold) ÷ receipts × 100: the residual per HK$100 of receipts.
datasets.caveat: Aggregate accounting residuals, not net-profit margins, cash reserves or survival rates. Employment size does not identify chain ownership; retail shows a less consistent size pattern.

datasets.title: Sector counts cannot tell us where workers went.
datasets.summary: Employment and vacancies are different measures. Workable alternatives also depend on skills, pay, hours and care responsibilities.
datasets.caveat: Net sector changes do not measure layoffs, individual job transitions or causal border effects. The vacancy series does not track the same people as the employment totals.

datasets.title: Three measures of use. Three different meanings.

items.label: Eligible HA patients using follow-up pilot

datasets.summary: Connected care can involve coverage, payment, records and follow-up through separate defined arrangements.
datasets.caveat: Patients, attendances and record-feature users are distinct and potentially overlapping. Do not sum them or read them as a funnel, universal coverage or clinical outcomes.

datasets.title: Spending is forecast to move both ways.
datasets.unit: Additional annual consumer spending / S$ million
datasets.summary: The study forecasts about S$290 million net incremental outflow, alongside incoming visitor opportunities.
datasets.caveat: Forecasts, not realised spending, lost GDP or measured JS-SEZ effects. Rounded displayed inputs imply S$294m; retain the source’s approximate S$290m rather than implying extra precision.

future.name: SIJORI
future.question: How do changing industrial and tourism roles shape jobs, suppliers and household activity?
future.caveat: Distinguish Batam from Bintan. Sea-linked islands and historical divisions of labour are not forecasts for adjacent land-border cities.

future.name: Macao–Hengqin / Zhuhai
future.question: When do work and residence move together—and which services make that workable?
future.caveat: Specific institutions and entitlements differ. Repeated needs surveys are not necessarily household panels or causal evaluations.

sources.label: cooperation-zone authority's release on its 2024 social/livelihood survey

future.name: Mukdahan–Savannakhet
future.question: When does a bridge or freight corridor translate into locally accessible work?
future.caveat: Border towns differ from metropolitan labour markets. The 2009 ADB analysis models effects; distinguish it from empirical research.

future.name: Hekou–Lao Cai
future.question: How do relationships, intermediaries and border rules shape access to customers and information?
future.caveat: Qualitative borderland findings concern specific settings, not population estimates or a quantified return from social ties.

future.name: Greater Copenhagen
future.question: Who can use a mature cross-border labour market, and which barriers remain?
future.caveat: Nordic institutions differ. The cited OECD report focuses on third-country nationals, not all cross-border workers.

future.name: Grand Genève
future.question: How do earning, housing and service geographies distribute opportunities and public responsibilities?
future.caveat: Do not transplant fiscal formulas or assume the same causes of housing pressure. These are routes for further reading.
